paragraphs: Oral, Dental and Maxillofacial Surgery

Oral and dental health is very important both in itself and for overall good health. One of the key departments dealing with many issues related to oral and dental health is the oral and maxillofacial surgery department. In the oral and dental surgery department, which is a specialized field of dentistry, individuals are diagnosed and treated using oral, dental, and maxillofacial surgery instruments, effective surgical methods, and detailed analyses.

It is possible to apply to private or state-run healthcare institutions such as clinicals for oral, dental, and maxillofacial surgery. To understand what oral and maxillofacial surgery entails, it is necessary to know what conditions are treated in this department and what treatment methods are used. With this information, you can benefit from effective treatments by choosing reliable and comprehensive healthcare providers such as Dentaliva, which is among the oral and maxillofacial surgery clinics.
## What Does Oral, Dental, and Maxillofacial Surgery Treat?

Oral, dental, and maxillofacial surgery treats many different health problems. As the name suggests, the oral, dental, and maxillofacial surgery department deals with health problems that occur in tissues such as teeth or jaw tissue and require surgical intervention. Unlike fields such as jaw surgery endodontics or classical dentistry, it is a department that treats much more complex cases with effective interventions. People referred to as oral, dental, and jaw surgery doctors are also dentists. However, these individuals complete a 5-year education in dentistry and then undergo an additional 4-year specialty training in oral, dental, and maxillofacial surgery. Upon successfully passing the DUS (Specialty Exam for Dentists) as a result of this training, they become oral, dental, and maxillofacial surgery specialists and provide services in this field in addition to dentistry.
### Diseases Treated by Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery

Contrary to popular belief, oral and maxillofacial surgery is a field that deals with many health problems, not just one or a few. Some of the health problems frequently addressed in the field of oral and maxillofacial surgery can be explained in a few points.

Although many people are unaware of it, impacted teeth are actually a very important problem. If a tooth remains impacted, meaning that despite the presence of the tooth root and the need for it to erupt, it cannot erupt, this situation negatively affects other surrounding teeth and even tissues such as the jaw joint and soft tissue. While impacted teeth in children can be resolved by methods such as extracting baby teeth to make room for the existing tooth, in adults, it must be resolved with medical materials such as oral and maxillofacial surgery instruments and effective surgical interventions. In particular, impacted wisdom teeth are a very common condition and an important problem that must be addressed by an oral and maxillofacial surgeon.

Cysts may form in the jaw region, both in bone tissue and in other tissues that can be referred to as soft tissue. Some cysts are congenital, while others may develop later in life. It is particularly important and necessary to remove solid and malignant cysts using jaw surgery methods in order to preserve the jaw structure and keep the general health condition under control.

Jaw joint disorders, medically known as TMD disorders, are health problems that are usually congenital. However, in some cases, factors such as facial paralysis or traumatic accidents can also cause temporomandibular joint disorders to occur later in life. Temporomandibular joint disorders can lead to many different problems, ranging from restricted mouth movement to clicking sounds from the joint, headaches, and jaw locking. For this reason, temporomandibular joint disorders must be treated in the field of oral and maxillofacial surgery, which addresses this health problem.
## The Importance of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery

Oral and maxillofacial surgery is very important for many different reasons. It is not possible to treat all kinds of problems related to oral and dental health with limited methods such as classic dental treatments. At this point, jaw surgery methods come into play, making it possible to treat very important health problems such as impacted teeth or jaw joint disorders in an ideal, personalized, and correct manner. For all these reasons, it is important not to overlook the importance of the oral, dental, and maxillofacial surgery department, just like other health departments and dental specialties.
## Does Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery Apply Braces?

Oral and maxillofacial surgery does not apply braces. Applying braces, i.e., wire treatment performed to align teeth correctly, is generally a treatment handled in the field of orthodontics. However, in rare cases, oral and maxillofacial surgeons and orthodontists may consult and jointly decide on braces treatment. Individuals who need braces treatment due to problems requiring surgical intervention in the jaw should first consult the oral and maxillofacial surgery department.

In order to receive appropriate, reliable, and correct treatment in oral, dental, and maxillofacial surgery, you need to make the right choice of clinic for maxillofacial surgery. When trying to make an appointment for oral, dental, and maxillofacial surgery, you may come across many different healthcare facility options. Unfortunately, some of these institutions are not officially recognized as healthcare institutions, meaning they have not obtained the necessary permits from the Ministry of Health and do not meet the required standards. You should avoid such institutions and choose reliable and satisfactory service providers such as Dentaliva for your oral and maxillofacial surgery appointment. By booking an appointment directly with Dentaliva for oral and maxillofacial surgery, you can benefit from comprehensive and professional healthcare services without wasting time.
## The Most Common Treatments in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery

Multiple treatments are performed in the field of oral and maxillofacial surgery. The most common treatment methods in the field of oral and maxillofacial surgery can be categorized under several headings.
### Impacted Tooth Treatment

Impacted tooth treatment is usually performed on adults as a result of impacted wisdom teeth, but it can also be performed in other situations, albeit rarely. In impacted tooth treatment, imaging techniques such as panoramic X-rays are first used to obtain information about the position of the tooth or teeth in question. Based on this information, a detailed plan is made, and the surgical intervention phase begins. During the surgical intervention phase, local anesthesia is usually used to prevent the patient from feeling pain. After local anesthesia is administered, an incision is made, and the impacted tooth is removed in pieces or whole, depending on the situation. Special materials known as oral and maxillofacial surgery instruments are used in impacted tooth treatment, allowing treatment to be performed without damaging other surrounding tissues and teeth.
### Implant Treatments

Another type of treatment frequently performed in the oral and maxillofacial surgery department is implant treatment. Especially in comprehensive implant treatments, jaw surgery expertise is required because delicate surgical intervention is necessary. In implant treatment, artificial tooth roots are placed in the gum tissue and jawbone, permanently, safely, and comfortably solving individuals’ toothlessness problems.
### Treatment of Cysts in the Mouth and Jaw Areas

Another treatment frequently performed in the oral and maxillofacial surgery department is the treatment of cysts in the mouth and jaw area. In particular, a maxillofacial surgeon and their expertise are needed to remove malignant cysts and, in this context, to perform biopsies on benign cysts to determine whether they are benign or malignant. Cysts in the mouth and jaw areas can be treated correctly with operations performed by maxillofacial surgeons.

Jaw injuries can also be treated in the field of oral and maxillofacial surgery. Especially in cases of trauma involving a hard blow to the mouth and jaw area, it is necessary to consult the oral, dental, and maxillofacial surgery department. In cases such as a broken jawbone or various types of damage to the joints, treatment is performed through closed or open surgery.

blocks.text: Emergency Dental Treatment Situations in Children

Pedodontics is a pediatric field concerned with children’s oral and dental health. Dental treatments for children are performed within the scope of pedodontics. Although many people overlook it, children’s oral and dental health is just as important as that of adults. In fact, in some cases, oral and dental health problems experienced in childhood can even pave the way for certain health problems in adulthood. Therefore, dental treatment in young children should not be neglected, and especially when emergency dental treatment is necessary in children, this situation should not be overlooked.

Some individuals are unaware that methods such as fillings for young children are used, thinking that children’s baby teeth, or in other words, temporary teeth, are insignificant. However, when deemed necessary by a specialist emergency pediatric dentist, many interventions can be performed, ranging from fillings to baby teeth to other treatment methods.
When is Emergency Dental Treatment Necessary for Children?

There are several situations that may prompt you to seek an emergency dentist for your child. The circumstances that necessitate emergency dental treatment for children can be explained in detail under several headings.
Broken Teeth

Broken teeth are much more common in children than in adults. The main reason for this is that children are physically much more active and uncontrolled than adults. In addition, factors such as the fragility of sensitive teeth, such as baby teeth, have also contributed to tooth fractures being much more common in children than in adults. Tooth fractures in children can occur in both baby teeth and permanent teeth. In both cases, it is necessary to see a dentist immediately. Especially if the fracture is very deep, damages the internal structure of the tooth, and there is a risk of life-threatening situations, such as the broken piece coming loose and entering the child’s windpipe, you should see a pediatric dentist immediately, without worrying about issues such as the cost of pediatric dental trauma. Otherwise, your child may suffer permanent damage to their teeth and even be at risk of life-threatening situations.
Complete Displacement of the Tooth (Avulsion)

Another condition commonly seen in children that requires emergency dental treatment is the complete displacement of the tooth, medically known as avulsion. Both baby teeth and permanent teeth can become dislodged in cases of avulsion. Many situations, such as trauma or problems with tooth development, can cause a tooth to become dislodged. In such cases, it may be possible to reinsert the tooth back into its socket, which is quite remarkable. Therefore, especially if a permanent tooth becomes dislodged, you should consult a dentist without delay. When visiting professional healthcare institutions such as Dentaliva, which is among the children’s dental emergency clinic options in Istanbul, and visiting a specialist emergency pediatric dentist, you should take the dislodged tooth with you. However, when taking the tooth with you, you should take care not to damage the root of the tooth and, if possible, keep the tooth moist. This way, you can keep the tooth alive and have it reinserted into your child’s mouth.
Tooth Displacement (Luxation)

Another situation that requires emergency dental treatment is tooth displacement, medically known as luxation. Commonly referred to as a loose tooth, this condition is quite dangerous because it causes the tooth to shift from its axis in a different direction, and it is a situation that requires emergency dental treatment, especially in children. Children are at greater risk for oral trauma and, because their teeth are still developing, they are at greater risk than adults for tooth displacement. The displacement of baby teeth inward or outward directly leads to the need for treatment such as tooth extraction, while the occurrence of such problems in permanent teeth leads to the need for more urgent and complex treatments. Dislocation can also cause toothache in children.
Tooth Decay

Many people consider tooth decay in children to be normal and believe that no treatment is necessary, especially when baby teeth decay. However, this is not actually the case. Decay in both baby teeth and permanent teeth in children requires treatment. Although baby teeth are temporary, cavities in these teeth can jeopardize overall oral health. Cavities in permanent teeth can lead to the loss of a tooth that a child could use throughout their life. For all these reasons, when tooth decay is involved, dental fillings for young children should be considered. One of the most economical treatments within the scope of dental treatments for children is decay treatment, and this is clearly evident when considering the emergency pediatric dentistry fee and emergency children’s dental treatment prices.
Other Emergency Situations Requiring Emergency Dental Treatment in Children and What to Do

Emergency dental treatment in children is not limited to visible problems such as tooth decay and broken teeth. There may also be different problems that are not visible on the surface but manifest themselves through certain symptoms. In situations requiring emergency dental treatment in children, you need to consult a specialist emergency pediatric dentist. In this context, you can choose reliable healthcare institutions such as Dentaliva, which is among the pediatric dental emergency clinic Istanbul options. Other situations indicating the need for emergency dental treatment in children can be addressed under several headings.
Severe Toothache and Facial Swelling

Severe toothache and facial swelling, just like in adults, are usually signs of dental infections in children. Therefore, if your child’s tooth hurts a lot and is accompanied by symptoms such as facial swelling, you need to seek immediate medical attention.
Soft Tissue Injuries Inside the Mouth

Another problem requiring urgent treatment in children is injury to the soft tissues inside the mouth. If symptoms such as deep bleeding are seen in tissues such as the tongue or gum tissue, it is necessary to consult a specialist emergency pediatric dentist immediately.
Problems Related to Braces

The use of braces is much more common in children than in adults, and therefore problems related to braces are also frequently seen in children. For example, many situations, such as damage to tissues as a result of damage to the braces, can be remedied by methods such as repairing the braces as part of children’s dental treatments.
The Importance of Emergency Dental Treatment in Children

Emergency dental treatment in children is important in many ways. Although many people think that dental treatment for children is unimportant or unnecessary, these treatments are actually quite important and necessary. The reasons why emergency dental treatment is important in children can be explained under several headings.
Preventing Permanent Damage and Saving Teeth

A common misconception that leads to dental treatments in children being considered unimportant is the belief that children’s dental problems will not cause major damage because their teeth are temporary. However, oral and dental health must be considered as a whole, and it is very important and necessary for any structure in the mouth, including temporary teeth, to be healthy. Delaying a child’s dental treatment can lead to permanent damage and even the loss of permanent teeth that could last a lifetime.
Reducing a Child’s Pain and Anxiety

Unlike adults, children have much less control over their emotions and thoughts. Therefore, even minimal problems such as toothache and sensitivity can cause a child to feel very uncomfortable and even anxious. Thanks to the pediatric dentistry specialists at Dentaliva, one of the children’s dental emergency clinics in Istanbul, children’s physical discomfort, such as pain, can be treated with the right methods, and their anxiety can be alleviated with the right behavioral approaches.
Protecting Healthy Dental Development

Many people think that dental and oral health is very important for adults but not very important for children. However, children’s dental and oral health is just as important as adults’ oral and dental health. In fact, in some cases, pediatric dentists say that treatments aimed at protecting healthy tooth development during childhood are even more important than adult oral and dental health treatments in order to protect children’s oral and dental health in adulthood. Therefore, if you want to protect your child’s healthy tooth development, you should not ignore situations that require emergency dental treatment in children.
How Are Emergency Pediatric Dental Treatment Prices Determined?

Emergency pediatric dentistry fees, or in other words, emergency pediatric dental treatment prices, are determined based on multiple factors. Healthcare institutions such as Dentaliva, which is among the pediatric emergency dental clinic options in Istanbul, use various methods to reduce costs related to pricing, such as the cost of pediatric dental trauma, in order to provide services at affordable emergency pediatric dentistry fees. However, since the cost of pediatric dental trauma and the total emergency pediatric dentistry fee are determined based on the medical materials used in the treatment and the methods applied, it would not be accurate to provide definitive information on this matter. In summary, to obtain information on general topics such as emergency pediatric dental treatment prices or specific topics such as the cost of pediatric dental trauma, you need to consult a healthcare institution that provides services in the field of pediatric dentistry, such as Dentaliva.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can a 2-year-old child have a dental filling?

It is possible to perform a dental filling on a 2-year-old child. Although it may sound surprising, even a 2-year-old child can benefit from filling procedures with general anesthesia or local anesthesia when needed. However, filling procedures in children, especially very young children such as those aged 2, are quite delicate. Therefore, in some cases, the problem can be solved without filling or by resorting to methods such as tooth extraction. For all these reasons, whether or not a 2-year-old child can have a tooth filled depends on the situation and the dentist.
What should be done for a child with toothache?

First, you should approach a child with toothache with patience and kindness. You need to talk to them to make sure that a child who is very young and has not yet developed enough to express themselves is actually experiencing toothache. If you are sure that the child has toothache or if they say they are in pain, you should check for other symptoms such as swelling. If the toothache is accompanied by swelling, you should consult a pediatric dentist immediately. If the toothache appears on its own without symptoms such as swelling, you should consult a pediatric dentist as soon as possible.
How can children overcome their fear of the dentist?

How to overcome dental fear in children can vary depending on the situation. Some children may have traumatic memories of dentists due to reasons such as dentists’ inappropriate behavioral attitudes, incorrect use of anesthesia methods, or incorrect interventions. These memories can cause children to fear the dentist. In such a case, you can overcome your child’s fear of the dentist and convince them to undergo treatment by seeking help from both a pedagogue and a pediatric dentist who provides the right treatments.
How much do emergency dental treatments cost for children?

Since the prices of emergency dental treatments for children are determined based on multiple factors, it would not be accurate to provide a specific price for the total emergency pediatric dentistry fee or, more specifically, the cost of pediatric dental trauma. The cost of emergency dental treatment for children should be calculated taking into account details such as the experience of the pediatric dentist performing the procedures, the child’s medical needs, the treatment methods used, the medical materials used, and the facilities available at the healthcare institution where the treatments will be performed.

blocks.text: Dental filling is a comprehensive procedure used to solve many different problems in dentistry. Although many people think that dental fillings are uniform in terms of both material and application, this is not actually the case. A specialist filling dentist in Istanbul, as well as in any other region, can use different filling materials and procedures used in dentistry. Composite filling is a type of filling that stands out as the most preferred filling procedure. The fact that

composite filling procedures can solve many different problems, from tooth decay to appearance issues, has made this type of filling extremely popular. However, some unreliable healthcare institutions that may appear as clinical recommendations for composite filling applications can prevent you from benefiting from this popular application correctly. Otherwise, you may find yourself at a disadvantage, facing the destructive effects of incorrect application rather than the beneficial results of composite fillings. Who is Composite Filling Suitable For?

Composite filling is a filling material that can be suitable for many individuals. Composite filling application can be performed effectively to eliminate multiple problems. Also known as white filling, composite filling is a versatile filling material in terms of both aesthetics and functionality because it is produced from an acrylic resin mixture. The suitability of composite filling can be explained in detail under several headings.
Individuals with Decayed and Broken Teeth

One of the first uses that comes to mind when composite filling is mentioned is decayed and broken teeth. Teeth are one of the strongest structures in the human body, but no matter how strong they are, they can decay and break due to factors such as hygiene or external impacts. Tooth decay and fractures are not just superficial appearance problems; they are also health hazards that can damage the internal structure of the tooth.

Therefore, decayed and broken teeth need to be treated appropriately and reliably. Composite filling material is a material used in such cases due to factors such as its durability and freedom in shaping. For the use of composite filling in decayed teeth, the decay must first be cleaned, while in broken teeth, direct application can be made depending on the situation.
This preserves dental health, restores the aesthetic appearance of the tooth, and preserves the tooth’s functions.
Individuals Who Want to Improve Their Aesthetic Appearance

Composite fillings are a type of filling used not only for their durability but also for their ability to improve aesthetic appearance. This is why composite filling application is one of the first procedures used in comprehensive aesthetic applications such as smile design. With its color, texture, and ease of application, composite filling provides an effective solution for problems that cause aesthetic issues, such as gaps between teeth or discoloration on tooth surfaces. In some cases, aesthetic composite fillings can even be used as a covering material. This option can be considered ideal for those seeking an economical method, especially when the cost of a dental filling is considered to be lower than the cost of a dental veneer application.
How is Composite Filling Done?

How back or front tooth composite filling is done may vary depending on the situation. Since applications such as composite filling are used for both functional and aesthetic purposes, it is necessary to proceed in a manner appropriate for the individual. For this reason, the first step in composite filling is a comprehensive consultation between the dentist and the individual. During this consultation, information is gathered about the individual’s medical history and preferences. The information obtained is reinforced by the information the dentist will obtain as a result of a comprehensive examination, and a personalized plan is made before proceeding to the actual stages of the procedure.
Cleaning and Preparing the Tooth

When the actual procedure stages of composite filling are reached, the tooth is first cleaned. This tooth cleaning involves removing things such as cavities or layers on the tooth, depending on the situation. Since special materials and devices used in dentistry are used for cleaning, deep cleaning is ensured. After deep cleaning, a special gel is applied to the area of the tooth where the filling will be applied to ensure that the filling adheres.
Layer-by-Layer Application and Light Curing

The composite filling is applied to the tooth layer by layer. Otherwise, even if the best brand of composite filling is used, the shape of the filling may be distorted if it is not applied in thin layers. After layer-by-layer application, the filling material is hardened using devices that emit special blue light. Hardening the filling material is a very important and necessary process for ensuring the long life of the composite filling.
Types of Composite Fillings

Contrary to popular belief, composite filling applications are not all the same. Composite filling applications can be distinguished from each other according to their purpose and shape. Since back or front tooth composite filling applications can be performed according to the needs and wishes of individuals, it may be more logical to discuss composite filling applications under several headings.
Aesthetic Fillings Used on Front Teeth

The most popular type of composite filling application is front tooth composite fillings. Front teeth are at greater risk in many ways due to their location and various factors. Problems ranging from discoloration to the formation of tooth gaps, known as diastema, are frequently seen in front teeth. Unlike other types of fillings, such as amalgam fillings, composite fillings chemically bond to the tooth and even become part of the tooth, making them particularly suitable for aesthetic purposes on front teeth. For all these reasons, aesthetic composite fillings used on front teeth are one of the most commonly used types of fillings in aesthetic applications such as smile design.
Durable Composite Fillings for Back Teeth

Another situation where composite fillings are most commonly used is when a strong filling is needed for back teeth. Many healthcare institutions, including Dentaliva, which is among the composite filling specialist clinic options, recommend using composite fillings when filling back teeth. The main reason for this is that back teeth are used intensively for actions such as chewing, and therefore may require a very strong filling. Composite fillings can meet the need for strong fillings in back teeth because they bond chemically to the tooth.
How Can Composite/White Filling Costs Be Made More Affordable?

There are ways to make composite or, in other words, white filling costs affordable and benefit from a treatment that is not very financially burdensome. One of the easiest ways to reduce white filling costs is to choose affordable options when calculating the cost of dental fillings. When calculating the cost of dental fillings, many factors are taken into account, such as the individual’s choice of material type and quality. Therefore, you can make choices that will reduce the total cost of dental fillings. By choosing composite filling specialist clinic options that offer affordable services, such as

Dentaliva, you can receive services at affordable white filling prices. A clinic that adopts a policy of offering affordable services, such as Dentaliva, can create a treatment plan to offer affordable solutions even in a region with high prices, such as specialist filling dentist Istanbul. Specialist filling dentist Istanbul can plan to offer affordable services in a city like Istanbul, and you can also enjoy the benefits of receiving services at an affordable composite filling price.
What are the advantages of composite fillings?

Composite fillings are a type of filling that offers many different advantages. Composite fillings, especially when performed by a dentist specializing in fillings, can offer individuals advantages in multiple areas. Unfortunately, however, composite fillings performed under the wrong conditions and by non-dentists can offer more disadvantages than advantages. The advantages of composite fillings can be discussed under several headings.
Matching Natural Tooth Color and Aesthetic Appearance

Among the advantages of composite fillings, the most striking is that this type of filling matches the natural tooth color and provides an aesthetic appearance. Composite fillings applied in specialized composite filling clinics are also known as white fillings because they are white, which is the aesthetic tooth color. This provides a natural tooth color-matched appearance, especially for individuals who pay attention to dental health and have white teeth.
Quick Application and Economical Solution

Many dental treatments are performed in multiple sessions, which can cause the patient to lose a lot of time. However, this is not the case with composite filling applications. Composite filling procedures are usually performed in a single session, and this session is also quite short. The short session duration, the low composite filling price, and the simplicity of the composite filling procedure have all contributed to the affordable total composite filling application price. Therefore, composite filling is also an advantageous option in terms of offering an economical solution.
What Should Be Considered After Composite Fillings?

What to consider after composite fillings can be explained in two different ways: what to consider during the early recovery period and what to consider in the long term. What to consider during the early recovery period after composite fillings can be explained in a few points.
Do not eat after composite filling, and do not consume excessively hot, cold, or hard foods and beverages for the next few hours.
Accelerate the healing process by refraining from smoking and drinking alcohol for as long as possible after the procedure.

Do not perform any cleaning procedures, such as brushing your teeth, until the composite filling is completely dry. Even after the composite filling material has dried, do not use the tooth that has undergone the composite filling procedure for activities such as chewing very hard foods or biting things.
The Importance of Regular Oral Care and Checkups

Another thing to keep in mind after composite filling is to maintain regular oral care and undergo dental checkups. After composite filling, you need to add products that provide deep cleaning, such as dental floss and mouthwash, to your oral care routine. By visiting your dentist at least a few times a year, you can prevent situations such as the filling falling out and maintain your overall oral and dental health.
Frequently Asked Questions
Does composite filling cause pain?

Contrary to popular belief, composite fillings are not painful. In fact, most filling procedures are painless and comfortable. However, certain procedures, such as cleaning out decay before the composite filling application, may cause minimal discomfort. This minimal discomfort can be eliminated with local anesthesia. There may be slight pain after composite filling due to sensitivity, but this pain can also be controlled with strong painkillers.
Does composite filling solve the problem of gaps between teeth?

Composite filling can also solve the problem of gaps between teeth. Although many people think that composite filling is only suitable for filling cavities caused by decay, this is not actually the case. Composite fillings can also offer a solution to problems such as gapped teeth. Especially if you choose options such as Dentaliva, which is among the composite filling Istanbul clinics, you can quickly and safely get rid of gapped teeth or, in medical terms, diastema problems with composite fillings.
How much do composite fillings cost?

The price of composite fillings may vary depending on the situation. Multiple factors are considered when calculating the cost of composite dental fillings. The price of composite fillings can be determined based on many different factors, from the cost of the filling material to the experience of the dentist performing the filling. For this reason, if you want to obtain accurate pricing information about composite filling procedures, you should consult the healthcare facility where you wish to have the filling done.
Is composite filling maintenance difficult?

Composite filling is not a difficult type of filling to maintain. Unlike filling types such as composite filling amalgam filling, it is a type of filling that chemically bonds to the tooth, meaning it can become almost part of the tooth itself, so it does not cause individuals any difficulty in terms of maintenance. After getting composite fillings, you will not need to do anything beyond what is already standard, such as brushing your teeth regularly, adding products that provide deep cleaning, such as dental floss or mouthwash, to your dental care routine, and having regular dental check-ups.
How long do composite fillings last?

There is no standard lifespan for composite fillings. The lifespan, or more accurately, the usage period of a composite filling is determined by multiple factors. There are several brands producing composite fillings on the market. The quality of each brand’s products varies, and this affects the lifespan of the composite filling. In addition, factors such as how the individual uses the tooth or teeth with the filling can also affect the service life of the filling. However, on average, the service life of a composite filling is around 10 years.
How is a composite filling removed?

How a composite filling is removed may vary depending on the situation. Composite fillings are generally not self-removable because they are chemically bonded to the tooth and are therefore quite strong. Except in extreme cases, composite fillings need to be removed by a dentist using strong, specialized medical materials used in dentistry. Therefore, if you want to remove your composite filling, you should consult a dentist rather than attempting to do it yourself.

title: Bruxism (Teeth Grinding) | Dentaliva Dental Clinic

blocks.text: Teeth grinding, or bruxism as it is medically known, is a problem that many people are unaware of and overlook as a health issue. Bruxism is when individuals unconsciously or involuntarily clench and grind their teeth. This unconscious and uncontrollable teeth grinding usually occurs at night and during sleep. Bruxism can arise for many different reasons and is a problem that needs to be diagnosed and treated by scheduling a bruxism appointment, or in other words, by making an appointment with a professional healthcare facility.

Specialist dentistry also deals with bruxism. The specialist training that dentists who graduate from the dentistry department can obtain as a result of the DUS exam is quite important and effective in the treatment of bruxism. For example, a dentist specializing in pedodontics can intervene correctly with effective methods in the treatment of bruxism in children. In addition to all this, guidance from dentists can also lead to assistance from health professionals in other fields for the treatment of bruxism. For example, bruxism treatment with Botox can also be performed by a plastic surgeon. To obtain more comprehensive information about bruxism, it is necessary to be knowledgeable about many topics, from the types of bruxism to the causes of bruxism.
Types and Prevalence of Bruxism

There are basically two different types of bruxism. The first is sleep bruxism, which is much more common. As the name suggests, sleep bruxism causes individuals to clench and grind their teeth while they sleep, without even realizing it. Another type of bruxism is awake bruxism. Awake bruxism is when individuals clench their teeth uncontrollably while awake, even though it is uncomfortable, and in some cases, experience jaw spasms. Bruxism is particularly common in individuals who are prone to bruxism problems due to factors such as high stress levels and genetic factors. As a highly important field, specialist dentistry can address and treat bruxism problems in different ways depending on their type.
Causes of Bruxism

As with almost all health problems, there are multiple possible causes that play a significant role in the onset of bruxism. The causes of bruxism are crucial for determining the appropriate bruxism treatment and understanding the individual’s overall health status. The causes of bruxism can be explained under several headings.
Stress Factors

Stress factors are among the leading causes of bruxism. Stress resulting from factors such as intense anxiety, worry, and pace, referred to as psychological stress, also affects physical health. The effects of intense stress on physical health stem from both psychology and hormonal imbalance. Some individuals may develop various tics when under stress, and teeth clenching and grinding are among these tics. In addition, intense stress causes stress hormones such as cortisol to rise excessively, which paves the way for bruxism and has a very negative effect in cases such as increased jaw muscle pain. In fact, when looking at medications used to treat bruxism, it can be seen that most of these medications are psychiatric drugs. For all these reasons, specialist dentistry may refer patients with bruxism to different fields such as psychiatry.
Physiological and Genetic Factors

Although it may sound surprising, physiological and genetic factors can also cause bruxism. Conditions such as an imbalance in the jaw area or trauma that damages the jaw joints can pave the way for the development of bruxism. In addition, sleep disorders or certain health problems such as Parkinson’s disease can also lead to teeth grinding.
Bruxism Symptoms and Consequences

To understand what bruxism is and why bruxism treatment is important, it is necessary to be aware of the symptoms and consequences of bruxism. Bruxism symptoms and consequences are interrelated because the symptoms of bruxism often lead to uncomfortable problems in advanced cases, becoming linked to the consequences of bruxism. The symptoms and consequences of bruxism can be explained under several headings.
Tooth Wear, Fractures, and Sensitivity

Teeth grinding, or bruxism as it is medically known, has tooth wear, fractures, and sensitivity as one of its most significant symptoms and consequences. Teeth clenching and grinding movements cause the teeth to be under constant extreme pressure. Over time, this extreme pressure can damage all structures in the tooth, especially the enamel. In advanced cases, teeth may crack, break, and wear down, beyond just enamel sensitivity. One of the main reasons why teeth grinding treatment is so important is that bruxism can cause serious damage to teeth.
Pain in the Jaw Joint and Facial Muscles

Although many people are unaware, teeth grinding can damage not only the teeth but also other areas. One such area is the jaw region. Structures in this area, such as the jaw joint or facial muscles, can be subjected to excessive pressure depending on the individual’s teeth grinding habits and the intensity of this habit. Especially with the type of bruxism seen during sleep, individuals may wake up in the morning with unbearable pain and spasms in their lower facial areas, particularly in their jaws, due to clenching their teeth throughout the night. For all these reasons, another important symptom and consequence of bruxism is the pain and spasms seen in the structures of the jaw area.
Headache, Neck Pain, and Tinnitus

Bruxism symptoms also include tinnitus in addition to pain in the head and neck areas, which is actually a result of bruxism. Since the teeth grinding movement can strain many areas from the temple to the ear region, it can cause individuals to experience unbearable head and neck pain, as well as very uncomfortable tinnitus.
Decreased Sleep Quality and Constant Fatigue

Bruxism can cause individuals to experience sleep problems and, as a result, feel constantly tired, leading to chronic fatigue. In particular, individuals with sleep bruxism cannot sleep uninterrupted because they are disturbed by clenching their teeth throughout the night.

Not being able to sleep uninterrupted and sufficiently can also cause individuals to feel constantly tired and subsequently experience various physical or psychological problems. Due to this situation, bruxism treatment can sometimes be carried out with the help of psychiatric specialists.
How is Bruxism Treated?

Although bruxism is overlooked by many people, it is actually a very important problem and can be treated with different methods today. In professional and healthcare institutions that treat bruxism throughout our country, especially in Istanbul, interventions are carried out with treatment methods selected specifically for each individual and plans prepared specifically for each individual. When you look at the bruxism clinic Istanbul options, professional healthcare institutions such as Dentaliva use effective and reliable techniques as bruxism treatment methods. Bruxism treatment methods can be discussed under several headings.
Medication Treatment

Medication can be used in the treatment of bruxism. Certain types of medication that relax the jaw muscles are among the medications used in bruxism treatment. In particular, in the treatment of bruxism caused solely by psychological reasons, medications such as antidepressants may be used to bring the condition largely under control. However, medication is a treatment with somewhat limited effects among bruxism treatment methods and generally needs to be reinforced with other methods.
Night Guard (Occlusal Splint) Application

Plates can be used in the treatment of bruxism. However, unlike classic plates, the bruxism plate is a type of plate that acts as a retainer between the upper and lower teeth, ensures the correct alignment of the jaw, and can prevent teeth grinding. This splint is medically known as an occlusal splint. When worn throughout the night, the occlusal splint both prevents teeth grinding and ensures the jaw is positioned correctly. Therefore, especially when used as a bruxism treatment in children, the night guard can not only control bruxism but also promote positive jaw development.
Bruxism Treatment with Botox

Bruxism treatment can also be performed with Botox. Botox application makes it possible to temporarily and partially paralyze the jaw muscle. This temporary and partial paralysis can prevent the individual from involuntarily clenching their teeth. However, since the effects of Botox are temporary, if bruxism treatment is performed with Botox, the application must be repeated at certain intervals.
Other Psychological and Physical Treatment Methods

In addition to treatments such as Botox or splint therapy for bruxism, various psychological and physical treatment methods can also be used. Psychological support, or in other words, therapy, may be necessary, especially in the treatment of stress-induced bruxism. Through therapy, it may be possible for the individual to manage their stress better and break the habit of teeth grinding. For this reason, some dentists may recommend various psychologists’ clinics as a clinical recommendation for bruxism treatment, in addition to the treatments they perform themselves. In addition, physical treatment methods such as physical therapy exercises can also contribute to bruxism treatment with their positive effects on the jaw muscles.
What Determines Bruxism Treatment Costs?

Bruxism treatment costs are determined based on multiple factors. There are several main factors considered when determining bruxism treatment costs. The first factor is the preferred method of bruxism treatment. The main reason for this is that the costs of treatment methods for bruxism, such as the cost of Botox application and night guard prices, may differ from each other. The duration of bruxism treatment is another factor that has a significant impact on the price. As the name suggests, sleep bruxism causes individuals to clench and grind their teeth while they sleep, without even realizing it. Another type of bruxism is awake bruxism. Awake bruxism is when individuals clench their teeth uncontrollably while awake, even though it is uncomfortable, and in some cases, experience jaw spasms. Bruxism is particularly common in individuals who are prone to bruxism problems due to factors such as high stress levels and genetic factors. The causes of bruxism can be explained under several headings.
### Stress Factors

Stress factors are among the leading causes of bruxism. Stress resulting from factors such as intense anxiety, worry, and pace, referred to as psychological stress, also affects physical health. The effects of intense stress on physical health stem from both psychology and hormonal imbalance. Some individuals may develop various tics when under stress, and teeth clenching and grinding are among these tics. In addition, intense stress causes stress hormones such as cortisol to rise excessively, which paves the way for bruxism and has a very negative effect in cases such as increased jaw muscle pain. In fact, when looking at medications used to treat bruxism, it can be seen that most of these medications are psychiatric drugs. For all these reasons, specialist dentistry may refer patients with bruxism to different fields such as psychiatry.

Although it may sound surprising, physiological and genetic factors can also cause bruxism. Conditions such as an imbalance in the jaw area or trauma that damages the jaw joints can pave the way for the development of bruxism. In addition, sleep disorders or certain health problems such as Parkinson’s disease can also lead to teeth grinding.

Teeth grinding, or bruxism as it is medically known, has tooth wear, fractures, and sensitivity as one of its most significant symptoms and consequences. Teeth clenching and grinding movements cause the teeth to be under constant extreme pressure. Over time, this extreme pressure can damage all structures in the tooth, especially the enamel. In advanced cases, teeth may crack, break, and wear down, beyond just enamel sensitivity. One of the main reasons why teeth grinding treatment is so important is that bruxism can cause serious damage to teeth.

However, unlike classic plates, the bruxism plate is a type of plate that acts as a retainer between the upper and lower teeth, ensures the correct alignment of the jaw, and can prevent teeth grinding. This splint is medically known as an occlusal splint. When worn throughout the night, the occlusal splint both prevents teeth grinding and ensures the jaw is positioned correctly. Therefore, especially when used as a bruxism treatment in children, the night guard can not only control bruxism but also promote positive jaw development.

Bruxism treatment can also be performed with Botox. Botox application makes it possible to temporarily and partially paralyze the jaw muscle. However, since the effects of Botox are temporary, if bruxism treatment is performed with Botox, the application must be repeated at certain intervals.

blocks.text: Implant treatments are advantageous in many different ways and can offer solutions to many different problems. That is why many people want to benefit from implant treatments. The all-on-six implant treatment, in particular, is a type of treatment that appeals to many people, especially those who have lost all or most of their teeth. An experienced specialist 6 implant system can offer many different advantages to an individual with implant treatments.

However, if you make the wrong choice among options such as all-on-six implant clinics in Istanbul, you may encounter the disadvantages of all-on-six implant treatment rather than its advantages. Therefore, when it comes to clinical recommendations for all-on-six implant treatment, you can maximize the benefits of the all-on-six implant technique by choosing clinics such as Dentaliva, one of the first healthcare institutions that comes to mind. In addition to all this, to better understand what all-on-six dental implant treatment is, you need to learn many detailed pieces of information, from the differences between this implant and other types of implants to who it is suitable for.
What is All-on-Six Implant?

All-on-six implant is a reliable, effective, and comprehensive type of treatment that offers advantages in many different ways. With All on Six implant treatment, individuals who have lost most or all of their teeth can have teeth that they can use comfortably and durably, perhaps for the rest of their lives. Individuals who want to use both upper jaw and lower jaw implant-supported dentures can benefit in many different ways from the unique and advantageous features of All on Six implant treatment compared to other implants.
Differences from Other Implants

All-on-six implant treatment is a different application from other implant methods, primarily classic and single implant treatment. The differences between all-on-six implant treatment and other implants can be explained under several points.
Enabling the Use of Fixed Prostheses

Although fixed prostheses are generally used in single implant treatments, removable prostheses can be used in treatments involving multiple implants. However, the all-on-six implant treatment allows even individuals with no teeth to use fixed prostheses that completely eliminate the problem of toothlessness. The fact that the prostheses used in implant treatment are fixed and can only be removed by a dentist using special techniques ensures that the individual does not have to worry about their prosthesis falling out during activities such as eating or talking and allows them to use their prosthesis comfortably.
Patients with Low Bone Density Can Also Benefit

Under normal circumstances, in classic implant treatments, bone grafting procedures may be necessary for individuals with low bone density, i.e., jawbone resorption, to benefit from treatment, or the patient may be unable to benefit from implant treatment due to insufficient bone density. However, this is not the case for all-on-six implants. The All-on-6 implant treatment, like the All-on-4 implant treatment, is an innovative method that differs from traditional treatments. It allows even patients with low bone density to obtain implants and prostheses that they can use for life, thanks to the placement of implants, which act as artificial tooth roots, into the jawbone at specific angles.
Allows for Implant Treatment on the Same Day

Same-day implant treatment does not mean that the implants fuse to the jawbone on the same day, as commonly believed, but rather that fixed prostheses can be fitted on the same day. In classic implant treatments, prostheses are not fitted on the same day, or the prostheses that are fitted are removable, i.e., they are not fixed. However, in an innovative and comprehensive treatment such as the all-on-six implant, fixed prostheses are fitted on the same day to avoid inconveniencing the patient and to provide comfort. Once the implants have fully adapted to the jawbone, these prostheses are replaced with permanent fixed prostheses prepared specifically for the individual. The fact that All on Six implants allow implant treatment to be performed on the same day prevents individuals from worrying about issues such as the dentures falling out during the healing process after implant treatment and allows them to perform activities such as speaking properly.
Offering a Highly Cost-Effective Solution in the Long Term

All-on-six implant treatment is generally applied to individuals who have lost all or most of their teeth. For individuals who have lost all or a significant portion of their teeth, methods such as single implant treatments are economically disadvantageous solutions in the long term. The All on Six treatment fee can be considered a one-time payment, allowing the individual to gain economic advantages with the six-implant system they will use for life. For this reason, All on Six implant treatments performed at healthcare institutions offering economical solutions, such as Dentaliva, which is among the All on Six clinic Istanbul options, are a method that differs from other implant treatments in that they offer economic advantages.
Who is All on Six Implant Treatment Suitable For?
The All on Six implant technique is a comprehensive method that can address many different patient profiles. Who is suitable for All on Six implant treatment can be discussed under several headings.
Individuals Experiencing Complete Tooth Loss

The patient profile most suited to the All-on-Six implant treatment is individuals experiencing complete tooth loss. The All-on-Six implant treatment is seen as a method that is advantageous in many ways for individuals experiencing complete tooth loss and can meet many of the patient’s needs. For this reason, many specialists recommend the All-on-Six implant treatment performed with the 6-implant system for individuals experiencing complete tooth loss.
Patients with Low Bone Density

Another patient profile that benefits from All-on-6 implant treatment is patients with low bone density. Low bone density can be an obstacle to traditional implant treatments and may necessitate bone grafting procedures, but it may not pose any obstacle to All-on-6 implant treatment. Therefore, the All-on-6 implant treatment may be the ideal method for individuals with low bone density who wish to benefit from implant treatment.
Those Expecting Aesthetic Appearance and Functionality

The All-on-6 implant method is one of the most ideal options for individuals who expect to achieve an aesthetic appearance and advantageous results in terms of functionality from implant treatment. All-on-six implants, together with permanent prostheses, offer highly advantageous results in terms of both functionality and aesthetic appearance.
Those Who Want to Benefit Economically in the Long Term with Affordable All-on-Six Prices

When the cost of 6 implant prostheses is calculated, it can be seen that this cost is much lower than the cost of options such as dentures. How is All-on-6 Implant Treatment Performed?

All-on-6 implant treatment is a complex type of treatment and is performed in multiple steps. How All-on-6 implant treatment is performed can be discussed under several headings related to the stages of All-on-6 implant treatment.
Initial Examination and Personalized Planning

The first step in any implant treatment, including All on Six implant treatment, should be an initial examination. During this initial examination, the specialist determines whether the 6 implant system is suitable for the patient and obtains information about the patient’s general health. In addition, during the preliminary examination, the individual is informed about issues such as the choice of materials that affect the cost of the 6 implant prosthesis and makes choices. All this information is used to make a personalized plan, and the actual treatment stages are then carried out.
Placement of Implants and Application of Temporary Prosthesis

The actual treatment stages of All on Six implant treatment are the placement of implants and the application of a temporary prosthesis. In All-on-6 implant treatment, the specialist places the 6 implant system into the jawbone at specific angles, which differ from those used in classic implant treatments. This allows for highly advantageous results to be achieved with implant treatment. After the implants, or artificial tooth roots, are placed, a temporary dental prosthesis is fitted on the same day or very soon thereafter, depending on the situation.
Preparation and Fitting of Fixed Prostheses

In All on Six implant treatment, fixed prostheses are prepared while waiting for the healing process to complete after the implants are placed. These fixed prostheses are prepared in a laboratory environment in a personalized manner, taking into account factors such as the smile appearance the patient wants to achieve, the total All on Six prices, and the cost of 6 implant prostheses, as well as the materials selected by the patient. The fixed prostheses, prepared with great care and customized in a laboratory environment, are attached to the implants once the process of the implants completely fusing with the jawbone is complete, providing the patient with permanent teeth.
What Are the Advantages of All-on-Six Implants?

All-on-six implants are an innovative and comprehensive implant treatment offering advantages in many different ways. However, to maximize the benefits of this innovative and comprehensive method, it is necessary to choose reliable clinics such as Dentaliva, which is among the All on Six clinic Istanbul options. The advantages offered by All on Six implants can be explained under several headings.
More Stability and Maximum Comfort

The main advantages offered by All on Six implant treatment are greater stability and maximum comfort. Things to Consider After All-on-Six Treatment

There are several things to consider after All-on-Six treatment. You should pay attention to certain things in order to ensure a smooth early recovery process and extend the life of your implants and dentures. The things to consider can be explained in a few points.
After All on Six treatment, especially during the early healing process, you should clean the area where the implants are located with gentle movements and care products recommended by your dentist.
After implant treatment, you should avoid consuming very hard and crunchy foods.
You should completely stop alcohol and cigarette use during the early healing process after implant treatment.
Even if you experience no problems for the rest of your life after All-on-Six treatment, you should still have dental check-ups at least a few times a year.
After All-on-Six implant treatment, you should take care to maintain your oral hygiene once you have passed the early healing phase.

There is a widespread perception that all implant treatments, including the All-on-6 implant treatment, are very painful. However, this is not actually based on accurate information. During All-on-6 implant treatment, local anesthesia is used to prevent the patient from feeling any pain or discomfort during procedures such as implant placement. blocks.text: Aesthetic Composite Filling (Bonding)

Although many people think that filling applications and types of fillings are all the same, this is not actually the case. With the developments in dentistry today, different methods and materials are being used in filling applications. Aesthetic composite filling is one such application. Aesthetic composite filling is also known as bonding and has become a highly popular application today. Bonding teeth is an application generally used to solve aesthetic problems, which is why it has come to be known as aesthetic composite filling.

Aesthetic filling in Istanbul is a procedure that can be performed by many different healthcare institutions. Therefore, there are many different options that may come up as clinical recommendations for aesthetic filling. Some of these options are healthcare institutions that should not be preferred because they are not reliable and adequate. However, reliable healthcare institutions such as Dentaliva are excellent options for procedures such as aesthetic tooth filling. Choosing good options like Dentaliva for cosmetic dental fillings means benefiting from reliable and comprehensive healthcare services and getting the most out of cosmetic composite filling procedures in Istanbul. In addition to all this, to better understand what cosmetic composite filling is, it is necessary to know details such as how it is applied and in which cases it is used.
How is Aesthetic Composite Filling Applied?

How aesthetic composite filling is applied may vary depending on the situation. For example, there may be significant differences between the method of applying aesthetic composite filling for broken tooth repair and the aesthetic filling applied for the purpose of closing gaps between teeth. However, just like other cosmetic dental procedures, cosmetic composite fillings, or in other words, white fillings, require certain steps to be followed. The stages of bonding dental filling treatment can be summarized under several headings.
Examination and Planning

Although many people view cosmetic filling as merely a superficial application serving aesthetic purposes, it is actually a medical procedure. Therefore, as with all medical procedures, a comprehensive examination and planning are required before cosmetic filling. During the dental examination, the dentist can obtain comprehensive information about the individual’s teeth and overall oral health.

The comprehensive information obtained helps dentists perform ideal treatments in line with plans tailored to the individual. In addition, at this stage, the individual’s medical needs can also be met, ensuring they are ready for the aesthetic composite filling procedure. For example, some individuals may require various interventions on their teeth as part of broken tooth repair before undergoing aesthetic composite filling. Furthermore, the individual’s preferences are also taken into account during the planning stage. At reliable clinics such as Dentaliva, options such as FDA-approved filling brands and reliable methods are offered to the individual, allowing the process to proceed in accordance with their wishes.
Preparation of the Tooth Surface, Application and Shaping of the Composite Material

Aesthetic dental filling procedures cannot be performed without preparing the tooth surface. What needs to be done to prepare the tooth for aesthetic filling may vary depending on the patient’s wishes and needs. In some cases, the tooth may need to be abraded and made suitable for filling, while in other cases, the tooth surface may need to be roughened with medical gels. Making the tooth surface rough with medical gels helps to firmly bond the filling to the tooth during the tooth filling treatment.

Composite filling material is usually applied to the tooth in layers and shaped according to the needs of the tooth. After shaping, it is hardened, or in other words, fixed in place, using a special medical device. Depending on the situation, procedures such as cutting or filing excess filling material ensure that the individual achieves very positive aesthetic and functional results with the bonding tooth aesthetic application. Since these types of procedures are quite delicate and important, they should be performed by composite filling specialist dentists with the correct interventions, and as a final step, polishing and final checks should be performed.
Polishing and Final Checks

Polishing is, in other words, tooth polishing. In aesthetic composite filling procedures performed with the correct techniques using FDA-approved filling brands, polishing can be performed on both the tooth and the filling as the final step. Polishing makes the tooth and filling surface smooth and shiny. After all procedures are completed, final checks are performed. Final checks are very important and necessary because they help to understand whether the filling has been done properly and to make adjustments to ensure patient satisfaction. Therefore, when the bonding procedure is performed at reliable and professional institutions such as Dentaliva in Istanbul, comprehensive checks are provided as the final step.
When is Aesthetic Composite Filling Applied?

Aesthetic composite filling is a comprehensive medical procedure that can be used in multiple situations. The situations in which the aesthetic tooth filling application, which is quite popular among tooth filling treatment options, can provide a solution can be summarized in a few points.
Diastema (Gaps Between Teeth)

Spaces between teeth are medically referred to as diastema. Diastema is usually extreme gaps between the two front teeth and, more rarely, between other teeth. While diastema is congenital in some individuals, in others it can occur as a result of factors such as incorrect dental treatments or the influence of other teeth. One of the fastest and most effective methods available to individuals who consider diastema, or gaps between teeth, to be a problem is the application of cosmetic composite fillings.
Cosmetic Problems with Teeth

Many individuals face various cosmetic problems with their teeth. Many different situations, ranging from worn teeth to teeth that are too small, can bother individuals and be considered an aesthetic problem. Aesthetic composite fillings allow individuals to have a much more aesthetic tooth appearance and offer personalized, effective results through filling shaping, making aesthetic dental filling application ideal for aesthetic problems in teeth.

When it comes to tooth decay, especially small tooth decay, you can opt for aesthetic composite filling instead of traditional and non-innovative applications. With the bonding application, especially after small fillings are cleaned, the filling can be applied to the tooth in an aesthetic and functional manner.
What is the Difference Between Aesthetic Filling and Composite Filling?

The difference between aesthetic filling and composite filling is that these two medical terms are related but have different meanings. Composite filling is actually the name of a filling material, while aesthetic filling, as the name suggests, is the use of composite filling material for aesthetic purposes. In addition, because composite filling material is frequently used in cosmetic filling applications, these two medical terms have come to be used together. Cosmetic composite filling, or in other words, bonding, is, as the name suggests, the use of composite material as a filling for cosmetic purposes.
Advantages of Cosmetic Composite Filling

Getting aesthetic composite fillings offers many advantages. From the cost of aesthetic composite fillings being calculated at very reasonable prices to the quick solution they provide, many different features make aesthetic composite fillings an advantageous procedure. Especially if composite fillings are carefully applied by a specialist dentist, they can offer many different advantages to the individual. The advantages of the bonding procedure can be explained under several headings.
A Fast, Economical, and Tooth-Preserving Solution (H3)

One of the most important advantages of getting aesthetic composite fillings is that this procedure offers a fast, economical, and tooth-preserving solution. When compared to many other types of fillings, the cost of aesthetic fillings is quite reasonable. In addition, the fact that composite fillings are completed in a single session and in a short time by a specialist dentist, offering a solution that preserves tooth structure, is advantageous in terms of time, overall dental health, and aesthetic appearance.
Solving Many Dental Problems and Appearance Issues (H3)

Another major advantage of aesthetic composite fillings is that they can solve many dental problems and appearance issues at the same time. The fact that aesthetic composite fillings are customizable, meaning they can be shaped according to the patient’s wishes and needs, allows them to offer solutions tailored to individuals. For example, aesthetic composite fillings can provide solutions to problems such as discoloration and small teeth.
Things to Consider Before and After Aesthetic Composite Fillings

There are many things to consider before and after aesthetic composite fillings. It is necessary to be careful about many different issues, from choosing a clinic to what needs to be done during the early care period. Things to consider before and after aesthetic composite fillings can be explained in more detail under several headings.
Choosing a Clinic Before Aesthetic Composite Fillings

The most important thing to consider before aesthetic composite fillings is choosing the right clinic. Although aesthetic composite fillings may seem like a purely aesthetic and superficial procedure, they are actually a significant medical intervention. Therefore, you need to choose the right clinic before getting aesthetic composite fillings. If you agree with composite filling specialist doctors for bonding, you can manage the process in the most beneficial way.

In addition to all this, the choice of clinic is also an important factor in terms of bonding filling prices. While some clinics offer services at very high bonding filling prices, some clinics offer services at affordable aesthetic composite filling fees. If the bonding procedure is to be performed in Istanbul, you should choose healthcare institutions such as Dentaliva, which are among the Istanbul bonding procedure clinic options and offer services at affordable bonding filling prices. Otherwise, as a result of choosing the wrong clinic, you may end up receiving services at very high bonding filling prices due to some incorrect and unnecessary procedures performed by the clinic to increase the aesthetic filling cost.
What to Do to Extend the Life of Your Filling

To extend the life of any filling, including aesthetic composite fillings, it is necessary to pay attention to general oral health and to know that dental hygiene is not only achieved with materials such as toothbrushes and toothpaste, but also with dental floss, mouthwash, and dental procedures. In addition, during the early healing period and perhaps throughout the entire process of using the filling, as recommended by your doctor, you should avoid chewing very hard foods with the filled tooth. Otherwise, you may have to pay for the cosmetic filling cost and have to seek services from bonding clinics in Istanbul again due to permanent damage to the filling.
Frequently Asked Questions
How much does cosmetic composite filling cost?

The price of aesthetic composite fillings, or in other words, bonding prices, can vary depending on multiple factors. The main factors considered when calculating bonding filling prices are the experience of the dentist performing the procedure, the facilities of the selected healthcare institution, and the individual’s requests and needs. In addition to all this, the cost of aesthetic fillings can also affect bonding prices because the prices of FDA-approved filling brands can also vary. For all these reasons, you should contact a healthcare facility directly to get clear information about the cost of aesthetic composite fillings.
How long do cosmetic composite fillings last?

The lifespan of cosmetic composite fillings depends on many different factors, ranging from how the filling is applied to the patient’s oral hygiene habits, the quality of the composite filling material, and the capabilities of the healthcare facility where the procedure is performed. Under the right conditions and when performed using FDA-approved filling brands, aesthetic composite fillings generally last between 3 and 9 years. Factors such as the patient undergoing regular dental check-ups and not using the tooth with the filling excessively can extend this period slightly.
Can I smoke after getting an aesthetic composite filling?

Smoking after aesthetic composite fillings is quite dangerous. Many dentists recommend not smoking for at least a few hours or, if possible, a few days after aesthetic composite fillings because smoking can compromise the filling application and your overall oral health in various ways. Smoking delays the hardening of the filling, prolongs the healing process due to reduced blood circulation, and may cause staining on the filling. For all these reasons, try not to smoke for the recommended period after cosmetic composite filling.
Is sensitivity after aesthetic composite filling normal, and how does it go away?

Sensitivity after aesthetic composite filling is considered normal. Although many people think that aesthetic filling is a superficial procedure, important procedures such as intervention on the tooth enamel can also be performed in this application. Minimal damage to the tooth enamel can occur during procedures such as grinding and roughening the tooth, so minimal sensitivity may be experienced after the bonding procedure. There is no need to do anything to relieve this sensitivity because it will go away on its own within a short period of time.
